title: Mappingwise homotopy invariance of hammocks of simplicial pairs
statement: Use small simplicial categories and weak homotopy equivalences of mapping simplicial sets as in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. For an ordinary category $P$ with a wide subcategory $T$, write $H(P,T)(x,y)_k$ for reduced commutative rectangular zigzags with $k+1$ rows from $x$ to $y$: vertical arrows point down and lie in $T$, endpoint vertical arrows are identities, each horizontal column has uniform direction, leftward arrows lie in $T$, directions alternate, and no column is entirely identities. Include the length-zero diagram when $x=y$. Operators delete or repeat rows and then reduce by deleting identity columns and composing adjacent columns with the same direction. Composition concatenates and reduces. For a simplicial pair $(A,U)$ with a fixed object set, $\operatorname{diag}H(A,U)(x,y)_n=H(A_n,U_n)(x,y)_n$, with both simplicial operators applied together. Let $O$ be a small set, $A,B$ simplicial categories with object set $O$, and $U\subseteq A$, $V\subseteq B$ wide simplicial subcategories, also with object set $O$. Let $S:A\to B$ be a simplicial functor which is the identity on objects and sends $U$ into $V$. Suppose that for every $x,y\in O$ both $A(x,y)\to B(x,y)$ and $U(x,y)\to V(x,y)$ are weak homotopy equivalences. Then $\operatorname{diag}H(S):\operatorname{diag}H(A,U)\to\operatorname{diag}H(B,V)$ induces a weak homotopy equivalence on every mapping simplicial set. The map applies $S$ to each arrow and reduces. No freeness, cofibrancy, saturation or two-out-of-three hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, Lemma 2.4, printed p.20; proof in Section 5.6 via Lemma 5.7 and Sections 9–10 No Stacks tag states this simplicial-localization result.

proof.text: Fix $x,y\in O$. For a finite colored word $h=(S_0,T_0)$ and either $(C,W)=(A,U)$ or $(C,W)=(B,V)$, define $D_C(h)_{p,q}=G_{C_p,W_p}(h)(x,y)_q$. By [lem-coef-hammock-graph-colimit-presentation] the word operators compose columns in each fiber and insert identity columns for empty fibers. Applying a simplicial operator of $C,W$ to every arrow commutes with these operations because it preserves identities and composition; it also commutes with row deletion/repetition. Thus $h\mapsto D_C(h)$ is a diagram of bisimplicial sets for each of the two pairs. Applying $S$ to every arrow gives a natural transformation from the $A$ diagram to the $B$ diagram, since $S$ fixes $x,y$, preserves composition and identities, and sends $U$ into $V$. Set $F_A(h)=\operatorname{diag}D_A(h)$ and $F_B(h)=\operatorname{diag}D_B(h)$.

source.place: Definitions 5.1 and 5.3, printed p.24; explicit commutation of the two simplicial directions with the word operators

proof.text: For each $h$, its $+$ positions are $S_0$ and its $-$ positions are $T_0$, so $D_A(h),D_B(h)$ are exactly the fixed-word bisimplicial sets in [lem-coef-fixed-hammock-graph-homotopy-invariance]. All hypotheses of that node hold: the common object set is the given small $O$, the functor is identity on it, the distinguished subcategories are wide, it sends $U$ into $V$, and the two families of mapping-space maps are weak homotopy equivalences by assumption. Consequently $F_A(h)\to F_B(h)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every $h$. This applies the fixed-word lemma to its diagonal; it does not assert that $S_p:A_p\to B_p$ is an equivalence in each degree.

source.place: Lemma 5.7, printed p.24; Example 10.3 and Propositions 10.4–10.5 supply the strictly smaller fixed-word input

proof.text:
Take either $(C,W)=(A,U)$ or $(C,W)=(B,V)$, and put $F_C(h)=\operatorname{diag}D_C(h)$. For every $p$, [lem-coef-hammock-graph-colimit-presentation] makes $h\mapsto G_{C_p,W_p}(h)(x,y)$ proper in the signed-word sense of [lem-coef-proper-word-colimit-invariance]. For an injection $f:h_1\to h$, its degree-$n$ map $F_C(f)_n=G_{C_n,W_n}(f)(x,y)_n$ is therefore injective. If $g:h_2\to h$ is another injection and $h_{12}$ is their image intersection, the same ordinary properness in bidegree $(n,n)$ says
$$\operatorname{im}F_C(h_{12}\to h)_n=\operatorname{im}F_C(f)_n\cap\operatorname{im}F_C(g)_n.$$
These are exactly the two defining conditions for $F_C$ to be proper. Since $(C,W)$ was either of the two given pairs, this proves properness of both $F_A$ and $F_B$.

source.place: Proposition 5.4 and Definition 4.4; explicit degreewise check of properness of the diagonal diagrams in the Section 5.6 argument

proof.text:
The category $\mathbb H$ is small: its objects are finite binary words and its morphisms are functions between finite ordinals. Step 3 supplies properness of $F_A,F_B$, and Step 2 supplies the objectwise weak homotopy equivalences of their natural transformation. Therefore [lem-coef-proper-word-colimit-invariance] gives a weak homotopy equivalence
$$c:\operatorname{colim}_{h\in\mathbb H}F_A(h)\longrightarrow\operatorname{colim}_{h\in\mathbb H}F_B(h).$$

source.place: Proposition 4.5, printed p.23; applied to the diagonal fixed-word diagrams as in Section 5.6

proof.text:
For either $(C,W)=(A,U)$ or $(C,W)=(B,V)$, use [lem-coef-hammock-graph-colimit-presentation] to identify, in degree $n$,
$$\left(\operatorname{colim}_{h\in\mathbb H}F_C(h)\right)_n=\operatorname{colim}_hG_{C_n,W_n}(h)(x,y)_n\cong H(C_n,W_n)(x,y)_n=(\operatorname{diag}H(C,W)(x,y))_n.$$
Here colimits of simplicial sets can be constructed degreewise: form the set colimits, let their universal properties induce the operators, and check the simplicial identities on each cocone leg. Naturality of the cited reduction isomorphism for row operations and the operators of $C,W$ makes the displayed degreewise bijections simplicial. Thus the displayed formula identifies the source and target of $c$ with the two hammock diagonals. On a representative fixed-word diagram, $c$ applies $S_n$ to every arrow before reduction; this is precisely the map $\operatorname{diag}H(S)(x,y)$ which applies $S$ to every arrow and reduces. Every reduced diagram has a fixed-word representative, so the two maps agree in every degree. Step 4 consequently proves the claimed weak homotopy equivalence. Concatenation and reduction commute with applying $S$ because it preserves composition and identities; this also identifies the enriched functor. No freeness, cofibrancy, saturation or two-out-of-three assumption has entered.

source.place: Proposition 5.5 and Section 5.6, printed p.24; degreewise colimit/diagonal identification and comparison of the actual maps

Step 4: that node applies directly. Presentation node (DK 5.4–5.5): properness checked (insertions are injective, the intersection of insertion images is an insertion image); reduction is well defined (terminating, critical pairs close, each move is an 𝓘-morphism), so the colimit is the set of reduced hammocks; discrete and composite-identity cases checked.
